players.product: diesel standby gensets (95 L / QSK95) and QSK60 / HSK78 natural gas gensets for data centers; 130 L natural gas prime-power genset in development

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 and full-year 2025 headline results (CEO/CFO): Q4 revenues totaled $8.5 billion, an increase of 1%, 'as continued high demand in our global power generation markets, higher pickup truck volumes, and improved pricing more than offset lower North American heavy and medium-duty truck volumes'; Q4 EBITDA excluding $218 million of electrolyzer charges was $1.4 billion or 16% (vs $1.3 billion or 15.8% a year ago). 2025 revenues were $33.7 billion, down 1%, as lower North America heavy and medium-duty truck demand more than offset higher power generation volumes and improved pricing; EBITDA excluding one-time items was a record $5.8 billion or 17.4% of sales (vs 15.7% in 2024), with the 2030 financial commitments achieved ahead of schedule.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenues $8.5 billion (an increase of 1%); Q4 EBITDA ex-charges $1.4 billion or 16%; 2025 revenues $33.7 billion (down 1%); 2025 EBITDA ex-items $5.8 billion or 17.4%

quarterly_data.signal: Data center revenue (IR, Nick Arens): 'we had alluded, last call and $2.4 billion, $2.6 billion of total company revenue and expectations that would grow 30% to 35%. We did hit the upper bound of that. So for 2025, we are at about $3.5 billion between our power systems business and then also our distribution business.'
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 data center revenue about $3.5 billion (Power Systems + Distribution)

quarterly_data.signal: Power Systems (CFO): 2025 record revenue was 'driven primarily by demand for power generation equipment, especially in data center applications in North America and China'; EBITDA was 'a record 22.7%, up 430 basis points from 2024, driven by stronger volumes, favorable pricing, and a continued focus on operational performance margin improvement while improving capacity for future growth in demand'. Initial 2026 guide: 'we expect Power Systems revenues to be 12% to 17%, driven by continued strength in power generation and EBITDA in the range of 23% to 24%'.
quarterly_data.figure: Power Systems 2025 EBITDA a record 22.7% (up 430 basis points); 2026 Power Systems revenues 12% to 17%, EBITDA 23% to 24%

quarterly_data.signal: Distribution segment (CFO): 2025 revenues increased 9% to a record $12.4 billion and EBITDA was a record 14.6%, up 250 basis points, 'driven by higher power generation volumes and pricing'; 2026 Distribution revenues expected to grow 5% to 10%, 'driven by continued strength in power generation markets and higher aftermarket demand', with EBITDA margins in the range of 13.25% to 14.25%.
quarterly_data.figure: Distribution 2025 revenues a record $12.4 billion (increased 9%), EBITDA 14.6%; 2026 revenues grow 5% to 10%, EBITDA 13.25% to 14.25%

quarterly_data.signal: Initial 2026 outlook (CEO/CFO): total company revenues up 3% to 8% with EBITDA, including the dilutive impact of tariffs, of 17% to 18% of sales; 'Revenues in our global power generation markets are expected to increase 10% to 20%, driven by continued high demand in the data center market and the successful execution of our capacity expansion, which was completed in 2025'; China total revenue including joint ventures projected to decrease 1% in 2026, 'with weakness in heavy and medium-duty truck demand partially offset by growth in data center demand'. CFO: tariffs dilute full-year EBITDA by 'about 50 basis points' (mostly through sales and recovery, not dollar losses), and Power Systems JV earnings in China may be up a little.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenues up 3% to 8%; EBITDA 17% to 18%; global power generation revenues increase 10% to 20%; China revenue decrease 1%

quarterly_data.signal: Power generation orders (CEO): 'We had record order intake in Q4 for power generation. We are taking orders now well into 2028. So the demand remains very strong for diesel backup power'. Cummins does not quantify its back order, but 'we had a record in Q3, we set another record in Q4 in terms of that demand intake' with 'multiyear strength and continued discussions with our data center customers on how we can meet their multiyear needs'; 'We do feel pretty confident that we will see strong demand continuing for diesel backup power.'
quarterly_data.figure: record Q4 power generation order intake; taking orders well into 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and capex allocation (CEO/CFO): Cummins 'completed the doubling of our capacity of the 95-liter engine and genset that we supply, which is very popular in the data center market'; 'We are continuing to look at opportunities to increase capacity', with 2026 gains coming from the full-year benefit plus smaller efficiency improvements, and any additional capacity or new-product investments to be discussed at the May 21 Analyst Day. Investment planning 'as it relates to natural gas or other things' depends on 'having confidence in the multiyear outlook' and on 'our suppliers' abilities to invest and keep up with what we are doing in our own facilities'. CFO: 2025 capex included 'incremental capacity adds within our Power Systems business to serve the growing demand for data centers'; the total of the capex outlook 'in the last three months has not really changed, we have allocated more incrementally to power systems in the last few months' — 'we are a low-risk weighted play on the AI boom because we are making modest incremental internal investment for which there is high and growing visibility for demand.'

Power Systems Q4 and data center design (CEO/IR/CFO): the 95-liter capacity expansion was delivered ahead of schedule, so 'we saw more benefit of that sooner last year'; Q4 top line was held back by 'a few down days' typical at year-end, some aftermarket softening and a negative India tariff impact (IR: 'Q4 for power systems was more transitory impact of India tariffs coming through'; CFO, asked what the guidance assumes for India: 'we are talking tens of millions of dollars related to India', 'largely power generation markets where we are shipping products all around the world'). On data center design: 'there continues to be a desire for most, you know, really all data center customers to have diesel backup power available to just ensure a level of uptime and reliability that they need', with customer conversations 'more around how do we use the product line that we have to meet the strong demand that is out there'.
